_comment: Build and deploy configuration for the private MLflow tracking server.
Set the service's root directory to `ops/mlflow`. That makes this directory the
build context, so Railway finds ops/mlflow/Dockerfile at the root of it and
reads this file rather than the repository root's railway.json, which builds
the backend image. Same arrangement as frontend/.
Two settings are NOT config-as-code and have to be set on the service, because
Railway has no schema for either:
1. A volume mounted at /data. Without it the artifact directory lives in the
container filesystem and every report attached to a run is lost on the
next deploy. The tracking metadata survives regardless — that is in
PostgreSQL — which is exactly the failure mode that looks fine until
2. No public domain. MLflow's open-source server has no authentication of
its own, so a generated domain would publish every trace. The service is
reachable at mlflow.railway.internal:5000 over private networking and
nowhere else. The entrypoint refuses to start unless basic auth
credentials are set or MLFLOW_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=true states the choice
